matches.narrative: The Zebbies squeezed past Brighton Beach in a nail-biting opener, with Noah Jackson's two-goal haul leading the way and Nate Dooley and Fin Buttlin chipping in crucial majors. Despite struggling in the contested work with zero clearances compared to their usual five per game, the boys made their forward entries count when it mattered most. A thrilling three-point victory to kick off the season!

The Zebbies kicked clear for a solid 25-point victory over Mordi-Brae, with Noah Jackson snagging two goals and Tom Buck and Gill Davron each contributing majors in the 5.13 (43) to 3.0 (18) win. Jake Lansdown and Aidan Lynch were instrumental in the triumph, stepping up when it mattered most. A terrific team effort that sets up Round 3 perfectly!

The Zebbies secured a hard-fought 13-point victory over Prahran, with Hudson Schmidt and Nate Dooley leading the way as best on ground. Jack Gleeson and Morris Finch both snagged two goals apiece in the 48-35 win, while Dooley added another major to his outstanding performance. The team dominated the contested ball with 9 clearances and moved it beautifully by hand with 24 handballs received, laying 14 tackles to keep the pressure on throughout.

The Zebbies snatched a thrilling one-point victory over Beaumaris, with Jack Gleeson and Noah Jackson outstanding in the nail-biting finish. The team's defensive pressure was exceptional, recording 23 tackles—more than quadruple their season average—while doubling their usual clearance work with 6 for the match. Fin Buttlin and Morris Finch led the scoring with 2 goals each, while Jackson chipped in with a crucial major in the tightest of contests.

The Zebbies dominated St Peters with sustained pressure, racking up 32 tackles—more than triple our usual output—while our handball game clicked beautifully with 25 received compared to our season average of just 9. Jack Gleeson and Hudson Schmidt were exceptional in the 21-point victory, with Schmidt also finding the goals alongside Morris Finch's match-winning three-goal haul. Though we only managed one clearance, our intense defensive work and superior ball movement made all the difference.

matches.narrative: The Zebbies stormed past Brighton Beach with a commanding performance that saw them dominate at the contest, racking up 20 clearances compared to their season average of just 3, while Fin Buttlin led the way as tackles skyrocketed to 38 from a usual 14. Tom Buck was unstoppable up forward with 6 goals in a best-on-ground display, and the team's improved ball movement shone through with 29 handballs received—more than double their typical output.

The Zebbies dominated East Brighton with a commanding 32-point victory, powered by an exceptional midfield performance that saw clearances nearly triple from 6 to 17 and tackles double to 37. Ashton Fletcher led the goal-scoring charge with four majors, while Lewis Brauer and Raphael Knight were outstanding in the conditions, earning best-on-ground honours with their relentless work rate and smart ball use. With handballs received jumping from 15 to 27, the team's emphasis on sharing and supporting each other really paid dividends.

Despite the scoreboard, the Zebbies showed real fight against Port Colts with some outstanding individual performances from Nate Dooley and Patrick Whelan leading the charge. The boys won an impressive 39 tackles—nearly double our season average—and also exceeded expectations in clearances (10) and handballs received (21), showing they never stopped competing. Jake Crooks and Patrick Whelan hit the scoreboard in what was a gutsy display that didn't quite get the rewards it deserved.

The Zebbies absolutely dominated Ajax with a commanding 70-point victory, fueled by an outstanding midfield performance that more than doubled our season average with 21 clearances. Max Bahramis and Tom Buck were instrumental in our best-of-the-match honors, while Noah Jackson led a potent forward line with three goals, supported by two each from Patrick Whelan and Ashton Fletcher. Our players were everywhere, recording 29 handballs received and 31 tackles to completely control the contest.

The Zebbies dominated Mordi-Brae with a commanding 56-point victory, powered by Ashton Fletcher's brilliant six-goal haul and Xavier McCabe's stellar performance earning them both Players of the Match honours. The midfield fired with 16 clearances—almost double our season average—while 34 handballs received showed exceptional ball movement throughout the game. Fletcher led a potent forward line that also featured three goals from Noah Jackson and two from Lachlan Luckoff in an impressive team display.

Morris Finch was unstoppable up forward with five goals to lead our best-on-ground performance, while Raphael Knight was instrumental in helping the team rack up 16 clearances—well above our season average of 11. With 27 handballs received compared to our usual 21, the boys moved the ball beautifully all day in a victory that showcases just how far this group has come.

The Zebbies dominated from start to finish, keeping Beaumaris scoreless in an emphatic 54-point victory! Nate Dooley and Hudson Schmidt were outstanding across the ground, while the team's defensive pressure reached new heights with a season-high 43 tackles—well above our usual 25. Goals were shared around beautifully, with Lachlan Luckoff, Noah Jackson, and Michael Daly among seven different goal-kickers in a true team performance.
